subject: Onramp readout: success commitments & blocker ownership
messages:
From: Elaine Zhou <elaine@acmetech.com>
To: rafael_mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 4 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro / Redwood POC - quick recap

Thanks for the call this morning — good to meet the team. Quick recap from Acme's side and our high-level success criteria so we can align the POC: 

- Primary objective: Evaluate Redwood for low-latency embed-and-retrieval pipeline in our customer support search workflow.
- Success metrics (must-haves):
  - 95th percentile generation latency < 300ms for 1k concurrent sessions
  - Embedding recall > 0.78 on our dev set (we'll share eval script)
  - No customer-facing privacy leaks (data residency in us-east region)
- Timeline: 4-week technical trial starting as soon as onboarding access is available; target go/no-go by end of May.
- Compliance: we'll need a short SOC2 evidence bundle and IP/data handling confirmation. Procurement contact: procurement@acmetech.com (cc Marcus Reed).

Attachments from our side: acme-data-classification.pdf (pdf stub).

We'll rely on your MAP and a short risk/mitigation list to confirm the plan.

Thanks,
Elaine
Elaine Zhou
Product Ops, AcmeTech
elaine@acmetech.com
From: rafael_mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Zhou <elaine@acmetech.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben@redwood.ai>, priyom_das <priyom@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 4 May 2028 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intro / Redwood POC - quick recap

Thanks Elaine — great to meet you as well. Below is a short post-call readout from our side and the immediate next steps. I've attached a mutual action plan (MAP) and the initial POC outline.

POC scope (summary):
- Use-case: customer support retrieval + short generative responses for follow-up suggestions.
- Environments: hosted Redwood trial (us-east) with isolated workspace; optional dedicated capacity if throughput needs bump.
- Data: Acme will send anonymized dev set + eval script. We will not persist customer PII.

Success criteria (mapped to measurables):
- Latency: 95th < 300ms (measured on 1k concurrent sessions simulated by Acme load harness) — owner: Rafael Mendes (Redwood PM).
- Quality: embedding recall >= 0.78 on your eval set — owner: Marissa Cole (CS lead).
- Reliability: <1% error rate under expected load — owner: Ben Carter (Infra lead).
- Security/compliance: SOC2 evidence + KMS integration confirmation — owner: Priyom Das (Security).

Timeline (proposed):
- Week 0 (this week): access provisioning, mutual action plan sign, sample dataset ingestion.
- Week 1: baseline runs, initial latency/quality measurements.
- Week 2: tuning (quantization/batching), run full eval.
- Week 3: performance hardening + engineering hotfix window (if needed).
- Week 4: final readout & go/no-go decision.

Risk log (top 3 candidates):
1) Tokenization mismatch between Acme preprocessing and Redwood embedding pipeline -> may reduce recall (mitigation: shared tokenizer and sample payloads; timeline: 48h to validate).
2) Large prefix cache blowup under warm-up traffic -> may cause transient latency spikes (mitigation: rate-limited warmup and cache size tuning; owner: Ben).
3) Procurement delays for contract/DSA -> blocks access to certain envs (mitigation: short-term trial NDA & scoped MOU).

Next steps / asks from Acme:
- Send the anonymized dev set + eval script by EOD Monday.
- Confirm procurement contact and any required contract terms.
- Provide a primary technical contact for sample payload exchange.

Attachments: mutual-action-plan-ACMETech.xlsx (xls), redwood-poc-outline-v2.pdf (pdf).

Rafael Mendes
Senior Sales Lead, Redwood Inference

Adding an initial row-based risk/issue tracker that we'll update during the POC. I uploaded a CSV stub and included the first two entries below. Please review owners and SLA expectations.

POC Risk Register (initial):
- ID: R-001
  - Title: Tokenizer mismatch reduces retrieval recall
  - Impact: High (affects quality metric)
  - Owner: marissa_cole
  - Mitigation: Exchange sample payloads; run tokenizer parity check; fallback to server-side normalization.
  - ETA for validation: 48 hours after payload receipt
  - Escalation: Ben Carter -> Rafael Mendes -> VP Sales if unresolved in 72 hours

- ID: R-002
  - Title: Warmup cache causing 95th p95 latency spikes
  - Impact: Medium (performance noise during ramp-up)
  - Owner: ben_carter
  - Mitigation: Controlled warmup script; temporary autoscale policy; observability dashboard alerts.
  - Hotfix window: Week 3 (engineer on-call)
  - Escalation: Eng EM -> Infra Lead -> CTO (if > 24h outage)

Attachment: poc-risk-register.csv (csv stub).

Marissa Cole

Forwarding some technical notes after reviewing the sample traces Elaine sent yesterday.

----- Forwarded message -----
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 7 May 2028 09:10:00 -07:00
To: eng-oncall@redwood.ai
Subject: ACME tokenization/quantization notes

Team — quick summary: the sample payloads show tokenization differences (Acme uses whitespace-normalization + custom special tokens). That maps to a 6-8 point drop in recall on our baseline. Proposed immediate mitigations:

- Short-term: add a server-side tokenizer adapter that applies Acme's normalization (ETA: 48h). This is a configuration change and doesn't require a model recompile.
- Medium-term: include normalized tokenizer in onboarding SDK and add a preflight validation run in Week 0 (ETA: 1 week).
- Perf mitigation: enable prioritized KV cache with a smaller cache-size parameter during warmup; roll out via a feature flag.

Requests from Acme: sample anonymized failing queries and permission to run a few controlled A/B experiments (we'll share results).

Ben Carter
Infra Lead, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.ai

- Procurement will review the scoped MOU and aim to return a signed copy within 3 business days (Marcus Reed is primary).
- Technical contact: I'll loop in our infra lead for sample payload access (will share details separately).
